title: Benzene and Huckel's Rule Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
A snake biting its own tail, a round table sharing one plate, and mothballs with a strong smell all point to one molecule: benzene. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 9, Hydrocarbons) we learn why benzene refuses to act like three double bonds.

On the molecule bench, Kekule's two drawings blend into one resonance hybrid, X-rays show six equal 139 pm bonds, six p orbitals overlap and six pi electrons spread round the ring above and below it. Then Huckel's 4n + 2 rule link by link, a worked check of the cyclopentadienyl anion, and three ways to make benzene. Then the exam trap, an original JEE/NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 95 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.

In this video:
0:00 A ring, a shared plate, a smell
0:31 What is benzene
1:01 The molecule bench: Kekule and resonance
1:46 The orbital picture: delocalisation
2:27 Huckel's rule, link by link
3:09 Pause and think: naphthalene
3:30 Worked example: cyclopentadienyl anion
4:06 Preparation of benzene
4:35 Exam trap: cyclooctatetraene
4:58 Practice question (JEE/NEET pattern)
5:28 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Electrophilic Substitution in Benzene. How does benzene swap an H and keep its ring?
